subject: botany
question_text: Starch, cellulose, glycogen and chitin are polysaccharides. Choose the appropriate one and write it against each of the following: cotton fibre, exoskeleton of a cockroach, liver, peeled potato.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Botany Fastrack, Chapter 10 Biomolecules, book p.26, VSAQ 6. The book's four matches are standard and are used unchanged; the plant/animal grouping and the job each polysaccharide does are added as the reasoning. Only one source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both structurally impossible for this card, not merely unrun; 'not checked' here means exactly that, never 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Cotton fibre and peeled potato
lines: Cotton fibre is almost pure cellulose, the
material of the plant cell wall.
Starch is the stored food of the potato tuber.
steps.why: Both of these come from plants, and a plant uses cellulose for structure and starch for storage. Naming the job the polysaccharide does gives the reason for each match.
common_mistakes: Writing starch for cotton fibre. Cotton is cell-wall material, so it is cellulose.
Writing glycogen for potato. Glycogen is an animal store, not a plant store.
steps.memory_tip: In plants, cellulose is the wall and starch is the store.
steps.margin_note: Match plus one short reason for each. Two matches carry this mark.

steps.label: Cockroach exoskeleton and liver
lines: Chitin makes the hard outer covering of
Glycogen is the stored carbohydrate of the
steps.why: These two come from animals, and the same split applies: chitin is the structural one and glycogen is the stored one. So the four answers are two structural and two stored.
common_mistakes: Writing cellulose for the cockroach exoskeleton. Cellulose is a plant material.
Writing starch for liver. The animal store is glycogen.
steps.memory_tip: Two structural, two stored: cellulose and chitin build; starch and glycogen store.
steps.margin_note: All four items must be answered. A missing one costs the whole mark for that pair.

insider_note: This is a pure matching question. Write all four pairs in a list — no paragraph is needed.
